PLAN "Integrated 12-Week Fat Loss, Glycemic Control, and Phase 3 Push-Intensity Plan for Type 2 Diabetes (Metformin)"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Phase 3: push intensity increase to drive strength and hypertrophy while managing glycemic response"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Full-body foundation":
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          bent_over_row 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          overhead_press 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          leg_extension 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          leg_curl 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          chest_stretch 60 seconds
          hip_flexor_stretch 60 seconds
    WEEK 2:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Progression and technique":
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 3x10..14 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          incline_press 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_row 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          lat_pulldown 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          hip_thrust 3x10..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          calf_raise 3x15..20 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          shoulder_stretch 60 seconds
          thoracic_mrotation 60 seconds
    WEEK 3:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Volume build A":
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 3x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 3x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          barbell_row 3x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_shoulder_press 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          leg_extension 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          leg_curl 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          hip_opener 60 seconds
          quad_stretch 60 seconds
    WEEK 4:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Deload and technique focus":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          incline_press 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          dumbbell_row 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          lat_pulldown 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          hip_thrust 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          calf_raise 2x15 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          full_body stretch 120 seconds
    WEEK 5:
      DAY Tuesday training 60m "Fasted cardio morning":
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main cardio:
          walking 20 minutes rpe 4
          cycling 10 minutes rpe 5
        cooldown:
          light stretching 5 minutes
    WEEK 6:
      DAY Tuesday training 60m "Fasted cardio progression":
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main cardio:
          walking 20 minutes rpe 4
          cycling 12 minutes rpe 5
        cooldown:
          breathing_cooldown 2 minutes
    WEEK 7:
      DAY Tuesday training 60m "Fasted cardio maintenance":
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main cardio:
          walking 25 minutes rpe 4
        cooldown:
          hip_stretches 60 seconds
    WEEK 8:
      DAY Tuesday training 60m "Deload in fasted window":
        warmup:
          walk 5 minutes
        main cardio:
          walking 15 minutes rpe 4
        cooldown:
          full_body stretch 2 minutes

  PHASE "Phase 2" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 9:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Hypertrophy momentum":
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 4x8..12 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          bench_press 4x8..12 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          barbell_row 4x8..12 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          overhead_press 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          leg_extension 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          leg_curl 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          mobility flow 5 minutes
    WEEK 10:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Glycemic-aware progression":
        warmup:
          walk 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 4x10..14 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          incline_press 4x10..14 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          dumbbell_row 4x10..14 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          lat_pulldown 4x10..14 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          hip_thrust 4x10..14 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          face_pull 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          breathing_cooldown 2 minutes
    WEEK 11:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Strength & insulin sensitivity":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 4x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 4x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          barbell_row 4x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          overhead_press 3x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          leg_extension 3x10..14 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          leg_curl 3x10..14 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          hip_stretches 60 seconds
    WEEK 12:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Consolidation and deload":
        warmup:
          walk 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          incline_press 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          dumbbell_row 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          lat_pulldown 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          hip_thrust 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          full_body stretch 2 minutes

  PHASE "Phase 3" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 13:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Push-intensity phase start":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          bench_press 4x6..8 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          incline_press 4x6..8 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_press 3x8..12 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          overhead_press 3x6..10 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          lateral_raise 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          tricep_pushdown 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          shoulder_stretch 60 seconds
          thoracic_mrotation 60 seconds
    WEEK 14:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Push intensification continued":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          bench_press 4x5..7 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          incline_press 4x5..7 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_press 4x8..12 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          overhead_press 3x5..9 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          front_raise 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          skull_crusher 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          mobility_flow 5 minutes
    WEEK 15:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Push density and reach":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          bench_press 4x4..6 rpe 9 rest 120 seconds
          incline_press 4x4..6 rpe 9 rest 120 seconds
          dumbbell_press 4x6..10 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          overhead_press 3x4..8 rpe 9 rest 90 seconds
          lateral_raise 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          tricep_pushdown 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          shoulder_stretch 60 seconds
    WEEK 16:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Deload and technique polish":
        warmup:
          walk 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          bench_press 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          incline_press 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          dumbbell_press 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          overhead_press 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          full_body stretch 2 minutes

NUTRITION
DIABETES-SPECIFIC GUIDANCE
- Calorie target: continue moderate deficit 500 kcal/day from maintenance for Phase 3; reassess every 2–3 weeks.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight daily.
- Carbohydrates: distribute to support higher push loads; maintain low-to-moderate GI.
- fats: 25–35% of total calories; prioritize healthy fats.
- fiber: ≥25 g/day.
- hydration: 2.2–3.0 L/day.
- cheat meals: as in Phase 2, if desired, schedule after especially intense push days or rest days to aid adherence.
- intermittent fasting: optional; if used, align with clinician guidance and training schedule; maintain protein and macros within eating window.

MEAL PATTERNS
- Meals: 3 main meals + 1–2 snacks; align carbohydrates around workouts.
- Cheat meals: once per week optional; integrate into Phase 3 with attention to glycemic response.
- IF: discussed separately with clinician; can be compatible if glucose stability is maintained.

MONITORING
- Weekly check-ins; include push-performance notes (bench progression, reps, RPE).
- Glucose monitoring around high-intensity days as needed.
- HbA1c every 6–12 weeks.
- Cheating, IF, and any plan changes to be reviewed for impact on glycemic control.

SAFETY AND CONTRAINDICATIONS
- Prioritize form on heavier pushes; avoid gym injuries.
- Monitor for signs of overtraining; adjust volume if excessive fatigue or glucose fluctuations.

RESTRICTIONS
- All exercises use canonical vocabulary; no substitutions beyond safe alternatives.
- Cardio modalities limited to the listed options.

NOTES
- Integrated 12-week plan with Phase 3 push-intensity emphasis; diabetes-conscious nutrition and monitoring maintained.
- Coordinate with healthcare provider for any med adjustments, glucose management, or IF considerations.

PLAN "Pre-workout Breakfast for Fasted Cardio Days (12-week plan)"
TYPE guidance
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Support fasted cardio sessions with a safe, diabetes-conscious pre-workout meal"

RECOMMENDATIONS
  - Timing: consume within 30–60 minutes before fasted cardio or use a very light 5–10g carb option if tolerating. If exercising truly fasted (empty stomach), prioritize hydration and consider a small carb snack if energy wanes.
  - Protein: include 15–25 g protein to support muscle protein synthesis and satiety.
  - Carbohydrates: small amount, 15–25 g total, from low-to-moderate GI sources to minimize glycemic spikes.
  - Fats: keep minimal pre-workout to avoid GI distress; if tolerated, include a small amount (5–10 g).
  - Hydration: 200–300 ml water with electrolytes if needed.

SAMPLE OPTIONS
  - Option A: Greek yogurt (3/4 cup) + berries (1/2 cup) + a drizzle of chia seeds (1 tsp)
  - Option B: Protein shake with 20 g whey or plant-based protein + 1 small banana (medium)
  - Option C: Cottage cheese (1/2 cup) + sliced cucumber or tomato + 1 small apple
  - Option D: Oatmeal (1/2 cup cooked) + 1 tbsp peanut butter (optional small amount) + cinnamon
  - Option E: Hard-boiled egg + 1 slice of whole-grain toast + 1/2 orange

DIABETES-SPECIFIC CONSIDERATIONS
  - Monitor glucose response for first 1–2 weeks; adjust carbohydrate amount if glucose spikes or hypoglycemia occurs.
  - If on metformin, coordinate with physician regarding any fasting-related adjustments; hydration emphasized.
  - Prefer whole-food options with protein and fiber to stabilize blood glucose.

LOGGING
  - Track: meal type, portion sizes, time relative to workout, perceived energy, any GI symptoms.
  - Adjust plan based on energy during fasted cardio and glucose readings.

PLAN "Post-workout Snack Options for Type 2 Diabetes (12-week plan)"
TYPE guidance
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Support recovery and glycemic control with quick, diabetes-conscious snacks"

RECOMMENDED_SNACKS
  - Snack 1: Greek yogurt (170 g) + mixed berries (1 cup) + 1 tbsp almond butter
  - Snack 2: Protein shake (20–25 g protein) + 1 small apple
  - Snack 3: Cottage cheese (1 cup) + pineapple chunks (1/2 cup) or berries (1/2 cup)
  - Snack 4: Hard-boiled eggs (2) + baby carrots (1 cup) + hummus (2 tbsp)

  - Medical clearance: obtain clinician approval before initiating IF, especially with metformin and HbA1c 7.2%.
  - IF pattern options (diabetes-safe, adaptable to training):
    - 12/12 window: 12-hour overnight fast, 12-hour eating window (eats between 7am–7pm). 
    - 14/10 window: 14-hour fast, 10-hour eating window (eats between 9am–7pm).
    - Alternate-day fasting not recommended initially due to glycemic variability.
  - Training compatibility: schedule workouts toward end of the eating window or after a light fast, depending on tolerance and glucose responses.
  - Carbohydrate distribution: when fasting window is shorter, ensure adequate carb timing around workouts to maintain performance and avoid hypoglycemia.
  - Hydration: maintain non-caloric fluids during fasting; consider electrolytes if fasting duration is long.
  - Glycemic monitoring: check fasting glucose at start of fasting period and pre-workout; watch for hypoglycemia symptoms during fasting days.
  - Medication adjustment: consult prescribing clinician about any metformin timing or dose adjustments with IF; do not alter without guidance.
  - Protein target: maintain 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight daily; protein distribution should be aligned with eating window.
  - Fiber and micronutrients: prioritize nutrient-dense foods within window to meet fiber and micronutrient needs.

SAMPLE IF PATTERNS TEMPLATES (to discuss with clinician)
  - 12/12 with training in late afternoon:
    - Eating window: 12:00–24:00
    - Breakfast skipped; lunch around 12:00; workout around 17:00; post-workout meal by 19:00
  - 14/10 with morning training:
    - Eating window: 10:00–20:00
    - Pre-workout: small snack at 9:30 if needed; workout at 11:00; main meal after workout
  - 16/8 (more challenging; only with medical clearance and good tolerance):
    - Eating window: 12:00–20:00
    - Training aligned with first meal or after second meal as tolerated

POTENTIAL BENEFITS
  - May improve fat loss efficiency and insulin sensitivity in some individuals
  - Simpler eating schedule for some; potential appetite regulation

POTENTIAL RISKS
  - Hypoglycemia risk during fasting, especially around exercise or with metformin
  - Hypoglycemia symptoms may be mistaken for fatigue; ensure glucose monitoring plan
  - Nutrient adequacy challenges if eating window is too short

MONITORING PLAN
  - Weekly check-ins: weight, energy, mood, exercise performance, fasting glucose if available
  - Daily: track fasting glucose (if feasible), meals within window, GI symptoms
  - Adjust macros/calorie target if fasting affects energy or progress adversely
  - HbA1c recheck as clinically appropriate

RESTRICTIONS
  - Do not implement IF patterns that cause persistent hypoglycemia or significant energy drops
  - Maintain adherence to diabetes-specific nutrition guidelines and hydration
  - All exercise within the canonical vocabulary; no new exercise modalities introduced

NOTES
  - IF is optional and should be trialed only after medical clearance and aligned with current phase of training
  - If chosen, phase-in gradually (start with 12/12 for 1–2 weeks) before moving to longer fasts
  - Prioritize protein intake and fiber within the eating window to support glycemic control and satiety

          face_pull 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          breathing_cooldown 2 minutes
    WEEK 11:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Strength & insulin sensitivity":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 4x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 4x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          barbell_row 4x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          overhead_press 3x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          leg_extension 3x10..14 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds

        cooldown:

    WEEK 12:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Consolidation and deload":

          incline_press 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds

        cooldown:

  PHASE "Phase 3" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 13:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Push-intensity phase start":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          bench_press 4x6..8 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          incline_press 4x6..8 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_press 3x8..12 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds

        cooldown:
          shoulder_stretch 60 seconds
          thoracic_mrotation 60 seconds
    WEEK 14:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Push intensification continued":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          bench_press 4x5..7 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          incline_press 4x5..7 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_press 4x8..12 rpe 8 rest 90 seconds

        cooldown:

    WEEK 15:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Push density and reach":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes

          incline_press 4x4..6 rpe 9 rest 120 seconds

    WEEK 16:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Deload and technique polish":
        warmup:
          walk 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:

          dumbbell_press 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          overhead_press 2x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          full_body stretch 2 minutes

NUTRITION
DIABETES-SPECIFIC GUIDANCE
- Calorie target: continue moderate deficit 500 kcal/day from maintenance for Phase 3; reassess every 2–3 weeks.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight daily.
- Carbohydrates: distribute to support higher push loads; maintain low-to-moderate GI.
- fats: 25–35% of total calories; prioritize healthy fats.
- fiber: ≥25 g/day.
- hydration: 2.2–3.0 L/day.
- cheat meals: as in Phase 2, if desired, schedule after especially intense push days or rest days to aid adherence.
- intermittent fasting: optional; if used, align with clinician guidance and training schedule; maintain protein and macros within eating window.

MEAL PATTERNS
- Meals: 3 main meals + 1–2 snacks; align carbohydrates around workouts.
- Cheat meals: once per week optional; integrate into Phase 3 with attention to glycemic response.
- IF: discussed separately with clinician; can be compatible if glucose stability is maintained.

MONITORING
- Weekly check-ins; include push-performance notes (bench progression, reps, RPE).
- Glucose monitoring around high-intensity days as needed.
- HbA1c every 6–12 weeks.
- Cheating, IF, and any plan changes to be reviewed for impact on glycemic control.

SAFETY AND CONTRAINDICATIONS
- Prioritize form on heavier pushes; avoid gym injuries.
- Monitor for signs of overtraining; adjust volume if excessive fatigue or glucose fluctuations.

RESTRICTIONS
- All exercises use canonical vocabulary; no substitutions beyond safe alternatives.
- Cardio modalities limited to the listed options.

NOTES
- Integrated 12-week plan with Phase 3 push-intensity emphasis; diabetes-conscious nutrition and monitoring maintained.
- Coordinate with healthcare provider for any med adjustments, glucose management, or IF considerations.
